text:
Maya: quick sync — ran a 2h sample of production traces to validate the new workload-hash hinting for batching. initial take: length+decode-rate buckets reduce microbatch variance but we see tail latency spikes when KV priming misses :thinking:
Sam: can you paste the probe logs? curious about kernel handoff times and whether kv miss correlates with small batches
Maya: yep. attaching excerpt:
```
2026-03-14T07:12:03Z INFO  batcher: cohort=midlen-fast tokens=64 decode_rate=120ms kernel=wmma_fast batch_sz=8 handoff=3ms kv_hit=false
2026-03-14T07:12:03Z INFO  decoder: cohort=short-slow tokens=16 decode_rate=320ms kernel=scalar_fallback batch_sz=4 handoff=15ms kv_hit=true
2026-03-14T07:12:10Z INFO  batcher: cohort=long-slow tokens=256 decode_rate=450ms kernel=wmma_chunked batch_sz=2 handoff=40ms kv_hit=false
```
Olivia: hmm. long-slow gorups are killing tail. maybe our token-budget target (~48 tokens per bucket) is too low for mixed workloads so long requests force small batches and kernel choice flips to chunked kernels
Ben: agree. Also noticed that hash hinting sometimes maps similar-length prompts across different decode-rate bins because of jitter in early-step decode_time samples — that causes kernel churn. we should smooth per-session decode_rate with EWMA before binning
Alex: +1 on EWMA. propose: maintain per-session decode_rate_ewma with alpha=0.2, min_samples=3. then bin by (rounded_len_bucket, rounded_rate_bucket). reduces flip noise.
Maya: ran a quick sim with alpha=0.25 and bumped token_budget target to 96 for midlen/long. microbench: p50 latency unchanged, p95 down 18%, but p99 still high for very long seqs (>=1024)
Sam: any changes in kernel-selection counts?
Maya: yes — wmma_fast usage up 12%, scalar_fallback down 6%, chunked edges persist for sequences that don't fit kv cache patterns. suspect KV prefetch isn't warming because our priming policy only caches top-k prefixes per cohort; for long tails we need prefix-based heuristics keyed by prompt-hash prefix similarity
Olivia: can we try a cheap LSH on first 32 tokens to group prompts for KV priming? low-cost and should increase reuse for similar prompts
Ben: worth a probe. also want to try relaxed admission policy: allow batch formation to wait an extra 5ms for midlen-fast cohort when queue depth low — might avoid kernel flip by increasing batch_sz to switch to wmma path
Alex: tradeoff is added latency for some requests. run A/B on canary nodes and measure percent of requests that see >10ms extra wait: target <3%
Maya: I'll spin canary with: EWMA alpha=0.25, token_budget_midlong=96, admission_delay_ms=5 for midlen-fast, LSH-prefix-k=32, and kv_priming_topk=5. deploying now to canary pool (10% traffic).
deploy-bot: Started rollout to canary pool (10%) — rollout id rld-20260314-004. Monitor logs at /infra/logs/batcher-canary.
Sam: sweet. please post p95/p99 after 30m so we can compare vs baseline. if p99 doesn't improve, we should look deeper at kernel scheduling queuing jitter
Maya: will do — initial 10m numbers are promising: p95 -20%, p99 -8%. will report full 30m soon :rocket:
Alex: thanks team. if this stabilizes, we should fold EWMA + token_budget into default tuning and add a small dashboard panel showing kernel churn by cohort :eyes:
